about: Learning-owned (dc-r8-director20 R1): what Asha says around a child's aside, by kind of aside. returns: one question on {aside} the child can answer in a few words (what they like, what happened). replies: her answer to the child's reply, one slot {word} (a word of the child's, as said), never a fact, a taste of hers, a promise or a question. plain: the same with no slot, for when no word of the child's fits. Brain picks the kind from the aside's words (match), else 'other'. Validated by scripts/lesson-scripts/check.mjs asideReplyErrors.

sad.rule: Match whole words or phrases only (never inside another word: 'ro' is not in 'Roblox'). Not sad when 'nahi' negates it ('chot nahi lagi') or when the loss is the other side's ('dusri team haar gayi'). When the reply or the aside is sad, say one of these, never a {word} reply or 'wah', and ask no return that assumes liking or fun.

rules: {word}: only a noun the child said (sixer, Nobita, chutney, ludo, boat); never haan, nahi, pata nahi, kuch nahi, sab, a time word (kal, aaj) or an outcome (jeet gaya, haar gaya). If none fits, use plain.

{aside} in her line is in her voice and agrees: 'mera bhai' becomes 'tumhara bhai', 'meri didi' becomes 'tumhari didi', 'mere dost' becomes 'tumhare dost'; before mein / ke saath / ki / ka it takes the oblique form ('tumhare bhai ke saath', 'khane mein'); names (Maggi, Doraemon, Minecraft) do not change. Use the show's or game's own name, not 'TV' or 'youtube'.
A sad aside or reply (sad.match, by sad.rule) gets a sad reply and no return question.
If the child asks her back ('aapko kaun pasand hai?'), she states no taste of her own: a plain form, then the lesson.
